title: A mother's empty heart
hookLine: Musa's mother's heart became empty, and Allah steadied it (28:10)

cards: Pharaoh is killing the newborn boys of the Children of Israel, and a mother has just had a son.
By an inspiration from God, she's told to nurse him, and when she fears for him, to put him in a chest, as another surah tells it, and cast him into the river.
Don't fear, don't grieve, the verse says: We will bring him back to you. So she sets her baby on moving water and lets go. Surah Al-Qasas, the Stories, the twenty-eighth, begins Musa's life with her.

teach.b: The Qur'an doesn't skip over what she felt. Pickthall: "And the heart of the mother of Moses became void". The Arabic is farigh: emptied out, vacant.
Empty of what, commentators asked. Some said of everything except Musa; others, of patience, or of the calm she'd had the night before.
She was about to give him away, the verse goes on, to blurt out that the child was hers, had God not strengthened her heart.

The word there is rabatna, We tied: the verb for tying something fast so it doesn't drift. And the verse says why: so that she would be among the believers, those who trust. Notice what God doesn't do.
He doesn't take the fear away. Her heart is still empty; He ties it so that it holds. Then she does something very practical.
She tells Musa's sister, follow him. The girl watches from a distance as the child reaches Pharaoh's household.
God had kept him from taking any wet nurse, so the sister steps forward: shall I show you a family who will look after him?

So Musa comes home, fed at his own mother's breast, inside Pharaoh's household. The verse says it was so that her eye would be cooled and she wouldn't grieve, and so she would know God's promise is true.
In this telling, faith isn't the absence of panic. It's a heart held steady while it's still afraid.

how: Muslims read the story of Musa's mother in Al-Qasas as a picture of trust in God under fear, and many recite its promise, We will bring him back to you, in times of separation.

o: empty, like a mother's heart after the river
calm, settled, without any worry left
overflowing with joy at a promise kept

games.q: a mother's empty heart — tap the pairs.
p: We tied it, We bound it

s: the Qur'an says Musa's mother felt no fear
it says her heart became empty, and she nearly gave him away.
God strengthened her heart rather than removing the fear
rabatna: He tied it down so it would hold.
Musa was nursed by his own mother in Pharaoh's household
his sister pointed Pharaoh's people to her, and he came home.

games.q: you're Musa's mother. the chest has gone downriver. your heart is empty, and you could run and shout that he's yours. what do you do?
o: run to the palace and claim him.
tell his sister to follow him.
games.why: held steady by God, she sends his sister to follow the chest, and through her, Musa comes home.

practice: Think of someone waiting for something frightening right now: results, a court date, a child far from home, a hospital bed.
Hold their face in mind, and notice what they might need: not advice or cheerfulness, just someone beside them so their heart doesn't drift. If you pray, you can ask that their heart be tied steady.

wordCard.voice: Farigh. Empty, vacant: how Musa's mother's heart was left after the river, emptied of everything but her son, and held steady by God until he came home. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: empty, vacant; the word for the heart of Musa's mother in 28:10.

carryVoice: Your line: a heart held steady. Fear and trust can live in the same heart. That's five hundred twenty-four days.

sources.q: And the heart of the mother of Moses became void

sources.ref: Qur'an 28:7–13 (the river, the sister, the return)
